nodes.summary: The vector $y \in \{-1, 1\}^V$ with $y_i = 1$ for $i \in S$ and $y_i = -1$ otherwise. Goemans and Williamson pass between cuts and $\pm 1$ vectors through $S = \{i : y_i = 1\}$.
nodes.title: Sign vector of a cut

nodes.summary: For $m \ge 1$ and every vertex set $S$, $w(S, \bar S) \le Z_P$: the optimal value of the vector relaxation (P) in $\mathbb{R}^m$ is an upper bound on the maximum cut. No sign condition on the weights is needed. Goemans and Williamson state it as $Z^*_P \ge Z^*_{MC}$; the Lean statement bounds each cut, which is the same thing since there are finitely many cuts.
nodes.title: The vector relaxation bounds every cut

nodes.summary: For a vertex set $S$, the weight $w(S, \bar S) = \sum w_{ij}$ over the pairs $i < j$ with exactly one endpoint in $S$. The maximum of this quantity over all $S$ is the MAX CUT optimum.
nodes.title: Weight of a cut

nodes.summary: Every positive semidefinite $Y$ with unit diagonal is the Gram matrix of unit vectors $v_i \in \mathbb{R}^m$ for some $m$. With the converse, the semidefinite program and the vector program (P) have the same feasible objective values, once vectors of every dimension are allowed, so random-hyperplane rounding applies to any feasible $Y$. Goemans and Williamson obtain $m = n$ from an incomplete Cholesky decomposition…
nodes.title: Feasible matrices are Gram matrices of unit vectors

nodes.summary: At $\theta = \pi$ the ratio $\frac{2}{\pi}\cdot\frac{\pi}{1 - \cos \pi}$ equals $1$, so $\alpha \le 1$. A sanity check that the definition is not degenerate.
nodes.title: The Goemans–Williamson constant is at most one

nodes.summary: For $0 < \theta \le \pi$, $\alpha \le \frac{2}{\pi} \cdot \frac{\theta}{1 - \cos\theta}$. The ratio is well defined there since $\cos\theta < 1$, and it is positive, so the infimum is a real number.
nodes.title: The Goemans–Williamson constant is a lower bound for the ratio

nodes.summary: For a finite linearly ordered vertex set $V$, the set of pairs $(i, j) \in V \times V$ with $i < j$. Every sum $\sum_{i<j}$ of Goemans and Williamson runs over this set, so each unordered pair $\{i, j\}$ of distinct vertices is counted once and the weight $w_{ij}$ is read only for $i < j$.
nodes.title: Ordered pairs of vertices

nodes.summary: For every vertex set $S$ with sign vector $y$, $\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i<j} w_{ij}(1 - y_i y_j) = w(S, \bar S)$: a pair contributes $w_{ij}$ when its endpoints lie on opposite sides and $0$ otherwise. So (Q) is exactly MAX CUT.

nodes.title: Objective of the MAX CUT quadratic program

nodes.summary: The supremum $Z_P$ of the relaxation objective over families of unit vectors $v_i \in \mathbb{R}^m$. Goemans and Williamson take $m = n = |V|$; any $m \ge n$ gives the same value, since $n$ vectors span at most $n$ dimensions. The supremum is over a bounded set of values (bound); that it is attained, and computable to any precision in polynomial time by semidefinite programming, is not formalized here.
nodes.title: Value of the vector relaxation

nodes.summary: For unit vectors $v_i \in \mathbb{R}^m$, the Gram matrix $Y_{ij} = v_i \cdot v_j$ is positive semidefinite with unit diagonal, and its semidefinite objective equals the vector objective at $v$.

nodes.title: Objective of the MAX CUT semidefinite program

nodes.summary: A matrix $Y$ is feasible when it is positive semidefinite and $Y_{ii} = 1$ for every vertex $i$. The semidefinite program maximizes the objective over these matrices; its value is the relaxation bound $\mathrm{SDP}$ of the survey.
nodes.title: Feasible matrices of the MAX CUT semidefinite program

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$, let $e_0$ be the first standard basis vector of $\mathbb{R}^m$ and $y$ the sign vector of a vertex set $S$. The vectors $v_i = y_i e_0$ are unit vectors, and the relaxation objective at them equals the cut weight $w(S, \bar S)$. In the words of Goemans and Williamson, (P) reduces to (Q) for vectors lying in a one-dimensional space.
nodes.title: Cuts embed in the vector relaxation

nodes.summary: For unit vectors $v_i$, the relaxation objective is at most $\sum_{i<j} |w_{ij}|$, because $|1 - v_i \cdot v_j| \le 2$ by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality. This is what makes the relaxation value a finite supremum.
nodes.title: The relaxation objective is bounded on unit vectors

nodes.summary: For nonnegative weights and unit vectors, every term $w_{ij}(1 - v_i \cdot v_j)/2$ is nonnegative, since $v_i \cdot v_j \le 1$.
nodes.title: The relaxation objective is nonnegative for nonnegative weights

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
